record.paper_title: Open problems in nuclear structure near drip lines
record.context_brief: Microscopic drip-line structure and halo physics
record.original_question: What is the correct microscopic description of nuclei at the neutron or proton drip lines when weak binding, short-range nucleon-nucleon correlations, long-range many-body correlations, and continuum coupling all matter at once? Within that description, does pairing suppress the spatial halo of weakly bound neutrons through an anti-halo effect, and how important are three-body interactions, such as Fujita-Miyazawa-type forces, in determining drip-line structure and isotope limits?

evidence.quote: Can these neutrons travel without the collision longer than stable nuclei? We need a microscopic picture of the nucleus at the drip lines, with full account of short-range nucleon-nucleon correlation and long-range many-body correlation in the continuum [18, 19]. Does the paring correlation suppress the halo effect (anti-halo effect) [20, 21]?
Furthermore, the three-body interaction might also play an important role at the drip line.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider atomic nuclei lying at the neutron or proton drip line, i.e., the boundary in the chart of nuclides beyond which an additional nucleon of the given type is no longer bound. Such nuclei are characterized by extremely small nucleon separation energies, by the appearance of spatially extended "halo" densities of the weakly bound nucleons, and by strong coupling of bound single-particle orbitals to continuum (scattering and resonance) states. They are also expected to be sensitive to short-range nucleon–nucleon correlations and to long-range many-body correlations.

Provide a unified microscopic many-body description of drip-line nuclei that simultaneously incorporates:
(i) realistic two-nucleon interactions including their short-range repulsive/tensor correlations,
(ii) long-range collective and configuration-mixing correlations,
(iii) explicit coupling of bound states to the particle continuum (scattering states and resonances),
(iv) genuine three-nucleon interactions of Fujita–Miyazawa type (i.e., interactions arising from the exchange of two pions with intermediate Δ-isobar excitation, and their chiral generalizations).

Within such a framework, address the following questions:

(a) Does the pairing correlation between weakly bound nucleons suppress the spatial extension of the halo density (the so-called pairing anti-halo effect)? Quantify, as a function of the single-particle separation energy ε and the orbital angular momentum ℓ, the conditions under which pairing renders the rms radius ⟨r²⟩^{1/2} of an ℓ=0 or ℓ=1 weakly bound orbital finite in the limit ε → 0⁻, and characterize the resulting density profile.

(b) Determine quantitatively to what extent three-nucleon forces of Fujita–Miyazawa type shift the predicted positions of the neutron and proton drip lines, alter the binding energies of the heaviest bound isotopes of a given element, and modify halo structure relative to a calculation using only two-body interactions.

State and prove the corresponding theorems, or provide a numerically converged ab initio calculation, that resolves (a) and (b) within the unified framework above.
artifact.status_search_result: The pairing anti-halo effect has been studied in HFB and three-body models (Bennaceur–Dobaczewski 2000; Hagino et al. 2017, 2020), with evidence found in odd-even staggering of reaction cross sections and in ³¹F. However, a complete unified microscopic description of drip-line nuclei treating short-range correlations, long-range correlations, continuum coupling, and Fujita–Miyazawa three-body forces simultaneously remains an active research program rather than a settled result. The role and quantitative impact of three-nucleon forces on drip-line locations is still under active investigation. The problem is therefore best classified as open / partially studied.

status_evidence.title: Pairing anti-halo effect (Bennaceur, Dobaczewski)
status_evidence.snippet: Original paper introducing the pairing anti-halo effect: pairing suppresses divergence of the nuclear radius for ℓ=0,1 single-particle states as binding energy vanishes.
status_evidence.claim: The anti-halo effect is established at the mean-field/HFB level but its full ab initio treatment with continuum and 3N forces is not.

status_evidence.title: New concept for pairing anti-halo effect as localized wave packet of quasiparticles, Phys. Rev. C 95, 024304
status_evidence.snippet: A three-body model interprets the pairing anti-halo effect as a coherent superposition of weakly-bound and continuum wave functions.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work (2017) continues to refine, indicating the question remains active.

status_evidence.title: Two-neutron halo structure of 31F and a novel pairing anti-halo effect, arXiv:2003.08044
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates the interplay of pairing, shell evolution and halo formation at the neutron drip line of fluorine isotopes.
status_evidence.claim: Drip-line halo/anti-halo physics in heavier systems is still being explored, indicating open status.
